meta.title: Can't your child say no? Here's why — and what to do | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to say no without fear, guilt or conflict. A game-based critical thinking course for kids aged 8–12.

hero.headline: Your child says yes — even when they want to say no?
hero.subheadline: They let others copy, go places they don't want to go, stay silent when their boundaries are crossed. This isn't weakness — it's a skill no one ever taught them.

media.alt: A child who can't refuse and agrees to things they don't want

pain.title: Not being able to say no isn't politeness — it's a missing skill
pain.body:
At school, in group chats, at the playground — someone asks, pressures, or acts hurt, and your child already says "okay". Not because they want to. Because they're afraid of looking bad, hurting someone's feelings, or losing acceptance.

This isn't about character. It's about manipulation your child can't recognise: pressure, guilt-tripping, "if you were a real friend, you'd help me". When there are no ready phrases and no inner foundation, agreeing is simply the easiest option.

The result: their boundaries gradually disappear, and others get used to taking advantage. The child builds up resentment but doesn't know how to change things without causing conflict.

solution.title: "Sila Slova" — a detective drama that teaches critical thinking
solution.body: 50 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to protect themselves.
bullets: 🔍 Recognises manipulation: pressure, guilt-tripping, "a real friend would help"
🧠 Understands why they say yes automatically — and how to stop it
💬 Has ready phrases to say no without conflict or guilt
🛡️ Can say no — and still feel okay about themselves and others

social_proof.quote: My son finally stopped letting the whole class copy from him. He just said no — and nothing terrible happened. It was a revelation for him.
social_proof.author: Marina, mum of 11-year-old Denis

faq.q: Is this a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at once. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
